title: When demand for labor rises

predict.q: Demand for software coders rises by the same amount in two cities. In City A, people can retrain as coders in a few weeks. In City B, training takes years. Where does the coders' wage rise more?

options.fb: Easy retraining makes supply elastic: new coders flood in, so employment rises a lot and the wage only a little.
Supply is inelastic in City B: few new coders can respond, so the wage rises most (12 → 15.33, against 13.25 with elastic supply).
The same demand shift gives a bigger wage rise where supply is steep, because few extra workers can respond.

task: Move the demand slider right by 200, then switch the supply setting from "inelastic" to "elastic" and watch We and Le. Compare the % change in the wage with the % change in employment for each setting.

target.do: Move the demand slider to +200 (try each supply setting), then press Check.

takeaway: When supply of labor is inelastic, a rise in demand mostly raises the wage; when it is elastic, it mostly raises employment.
